# Seeing quantitative data {.unnumbered}

::: {.hero}
<div class="eyebrow">MAPLE HILL SCHOOL · AP STATISTICS · 1.5–1.6</div>

## From an observation to a supported claim {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Build a graph. Read the pattern. Explain what the data show.

Read at your own pace, replay the constructions, and test your reasoning before revealing an answer. This interactive book accompanies our revised lecture on quantitative data.

[Start learning](individual-values.qmd){.start-link} [Open the histogram lab](histogram-lab.qmd){.secondary-link}
:::

## Your learning route

::: {.route-grid}
::: {.route-card}
**01 · Plot individual values**

Preserve observations with a dotplot or stem-and-leaf plot.

[Read the chapter →](individual-values.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-card}
**02 · Build a histogram**

Choose bins, tally responses, and draw one complete bar per row.

[Build a histogram →](histograms.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-card}
**03 · Describe the pattern**

Use shape, approximate center, spread, and unusual features.

[Describe a distribution →](describing.qmd)
:::
::: {.route-card}
**04 · Justify your conclusion**

Support a claim with numbers and context, without overclaiming.

[Worked examples →](worked-examples.qmd)
:::
:::

## One dataset, three views

Our running example is a **hypothetical sample of 24 students' one-way commute times**, recorded in whole minutes. Changing its display does not change the observations.

<div data-chart="commute-dot" class="chart-frame"><p>Commute times: 5, 8, 10, 12, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 18, 20, 20, 22, 24, 25, 26, 28, 30, 32, 35, 38, 42, 48, 58 minutes.</p></div>

## How to use this book

Read an explanation, try the activity, and then open **Show solution**. For graph-construction questions, draw on paper before looking at the completed graph. A correct count does not replace labelled axes, a sensible scale, and an explanation in context.

The activities run in your browser: no account, notebook kernel, or software installation is required. On a phone, open the chapter menu at the top. Your choices are not submitted to a teacher and are cleared when you reload the page.

::: {.callout-note}
## Keep the scope clear
Topic **1.5** covers dotplots, stem-and-leaf plots, and histograms. Topic **1.6** covers distribution descriptions and graph-supported claims. Standard-deviation calculations, formal outlier fences, and inference belong to later lessons.
:::

The site uses classroom-created explanations and graphs. Published datasets and exam connections are identified where used; original exam pages are linked rather than uploaded. [Sources and publication notes](resources.qmd).
